eras.name: Contenders
eras.sub: 2017–2023 · Blizzard's official tier 2, fed by Open Division and Trials, with academy teams for league franchises.

eras.name: The Open Circuit
eras.sub: 2024–2025 · Contenders ends. FACEIT League sits under OWCS, with promotion and relegation between them.

eras.name: Partners & FACEIT
eras.sub: 2026 · Partner teams lock in OWCS spots; FACEIT League Master is the road up for everyone else.

items.d: Blizzard announces Overwatch Contenders ahead of the league's 2018 launch, with open qualifiers in North America and Europe for Season Zero.

Promotion and relegation runs through Contenders Trials: top Open Division teams and bottom Contenders teams fight for the last spots each season. League franchises field academy teams such as ATL Academy and Fusion University.
The best Contenders teams in the world meet in Korea. Element Mystic beat ATL Academy to win the first Gauntlet title. ATL Academy's roster included Hawk and Sugarfree, who later played for Timeless.

The team's first org. Hour Zero wins Trial of Champions in October 2020, plays Contenders 2020 Season 2 and Gauntlet qualifiers, and earns about $2,700 before closing after Open Division 2021 Season 1.
The team's second org, between Hour Zero and Timeless, as the group kept growing. The stats sites have no public results recorded for it.
Contenders switches to the Overwatch 2 build and is overhauled to open up the ecosystem. Trials is retired.

Timeless debuts in the Open Division, co-founded by th3mfg and Chase. It grew out of the same group behind Hour Zero and Kaizen, with players and staff who had come up together, and became the biggest of the three.

community.summary: Co-owner Chase marked the first anniversary with a long thread calling Timeless a passion project. From the start the brand's time puns and #ShatteredTime tag gave it a voice most tier 2 teams didn't have.

items.d: Timeless takes Uprising Academy's Contenders spot, wins its group and finishes 3rd at Run It Back. A 4th-place qualifier sends it to the league's Pro-Am, where it beats Trick Room and takes a map off the Vancouver Titans, then finishes 2nd in the Spring Contenders Series.
For the final league season, Contenders teams can qualify for select league events, starting with a Pro-Am in the West.
Timeless wins the North American Flash Ops Holiday Showdown, beating Primis Tornado over seven maps. Roster: Sugarfree, Seeker, Hawk, Rupal and Vega.

items.t: Timeless Ethereal win Calling All Heroes
items.d: Timeless' team in the Calling All Heroes circuit, made up of women and players of marginalized genders, wins the championship. Its players speak publicly about how much they love playing for the org.
With the league gone, Contenders ends too. The new OWCS folds the whole Path to Pro into a single open circuit.
Most of the Flash Ops roster leaves for Toronto Defiant, so Timeless signs the WISP core plus SeonJun and OPENER. The new team upsets M80 3–2 and reaches the NA Stage 1 grand final.
A 0–3 loss to Citrus Nation ends Timeless' Dallas Major hopes, and the roster is released. Three days later TSM signs it, returning to Overwatch after years away.
FACEIT League becomes the tier below OWCS in NA and EMEA, split into divisions with Master at the top. Its Season 1 Master playoffs also act as Esports World Cup qualifiers.

items.t: Timeless qualifies for the Esports World Cup
items.d: With a newly signed team including Seeker, Timeless loses 2–3 to NRG Shock in the upper bracket, then beats them 3–2 in the lower bracket. That earns North America's 3rd EWC seed and keeps Shock out. Infekted joins on loan from Shock.

community.summary: The Infekted loan post, a Shock pun announcing a player from the team Timeless had just knocked out, reached 324.6K views, Timeless' biggest post. In the same week, ariel2, whose play had helped clinch the spot, was removed after community accusations of racist remarks. The qualification and the controversy hit the timeline together.

voices.gist: “Shocking the world time and time again.” The Infekted loan post.
Timeline of the qualifier, the roster removal and the loan.

items.d: The owners split over whether the brand should compete at the EWC. Most co-owners and most of the well-known social and creative team leave, many saying they won't cover the event. The Timeless Ethereal roster wins Calling All Heroes Minor 1 on July 7, then the brand goes on hiatus. The EWC roster is signed by NTMR, which plays the event in Riyadh.

community.summary: This was the most covered moment in Timeless' history, and the coverage was negative. Kryix reported that most of the well-known social and creative team left, many saying they wouldn't cover the EWC, and that staff felt left out of key decisions. A secondhand account (Namuwiki) claims the org expected EWC support money just from winning the seed and never applied to the Club Support Program. NTMR picked up the roster and the players made it to Riyadh.

voices.gist: “Out Of Time?”, the reported story of the exodus.

items.d: Timeless returns for NA Stage 3 by picking up the unsigned team Anomaly: Vision, Lukemino and squid, plus former Timeless Contenders players Doomed and cuFFa. It finishes 4th.

Down 0–3 to TSM in the grand final, Timeless brings in Lethal as a substitute and wins four straight maps for its first FACEIT championship. Two days later the team disbands, and Citrus Nation takes its OWCS slot.

community.summary: The “reverse sweep of the century” post credited every player, including Lethal, the substitute who came in at 0–3. Two days later the team disbanded, citing community confusion. Fans who had just celebrated the title were left asking whether Timeless was still a team.

items.d: The bottom OWCS teams now face the top FACEIT teams. In NA, Supernova and DhillDucks win promotion to Stage 2, while Amplify and Shikigami drop to FACEIT League Season 5.

Timeless returns with the WISP core, tops the Open Qualifier Swiss stage and opens the regular season by sweeping Team Liquid 3–0. A 3–1 playoff loss to NTMR keeps it out of the Hangzhou Major. On May 2 it disbands for good, and its OWCS slot, Rokit and Lukemino go to NTMR.

Partner teams get automatic OWCS places with no roster lock. FACEIT League Season 7 becomes the pre-qualifier: its top four in NA and EMEA skip to Phase 2 of the open qualifiers, which take up to 512 teams in Phase 1.
Disguised Toast's organization makes its Overwatch debut as one of the four NA partner teams.
As FACEIT League Season 9 NA Master champions, NTMR win the Stage 2 promotion/relegation event to reach OWCS NA Stage 3. Disguised stay up; The Kafe drop to FACEIT League Season 10.
Timeless reactivates its account and returns to competition.
Timeless, partnered with Missing GG, wins Calling All Heroes again. Roster: Sniper, sawhill, wsps, peace, zzz, NenWhy and scuffed.
The tier 2 season running alongside OWCS Stage 3, and the next route into the top flight for 2027.
